full_judgment:
Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the ad-interim Order dated 9-10-2017 passed by learned District Judge, Dhaka in the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 544 of 2017 staying operation of the notice dated 10-9-17 of termination of the Distributorship Agreement dated 26-11-17 should not be set aside. 

 5. In support of his contention he referred the case of Dainik Janakantha vs Sangbadpatra Hawkers 1 BLC 433, the case of Humayun M Vohra vs ESPN Star Sports reported in 55 DLR (AD) 99, the case of Sonali Aansh Trading vs Birla Tyres 57 DLR (AD) 117 and the case of Rajasthan Breweries Ltd. vs Stroh Brewery Company, AIR 2000 Delhi 450. 

 6. Mr Mohammad Ashraf Uddin Bhuiyan on the other hand appearing for the opposite party submits that as per section 7Ka of the Arbitration Act learned District Judge possess power to grant interim order which has rightly been invoked and as such the petitioner filed the instant revisional application without any basis. He submits that, meanwhile the opposite party has issued notice as per Clause 15 of the Agreement for resolution of disputes by appointing Arbitrator and since the cause is still alive and waiting to be resolved, learned District Judge rightly passed the restraining order. He next submits that opposite party has employed as many as 135 employees and as per law they have to be given 120 days notice to terminate their employment and in that event opposite party will sustain huge loss if injunction order is not sustained. He further contends that the petitioner terminated distributor-ship by letter dated 10-9-2017 without assigning any reason whatsoever and as such the order passed by the learned District Judge cannot be termed as Arbitrary. He referred the case of Crown Maritime Co vs Royal Boskalis NV 16 BLC 140 and the case of Drilltee-Maxwell Joint Venture vs Gas Transmission Company Limited (GTCL) 21 BLC 122. 

 8. So, far the termination of the distributorship of 9(B) is concerned, option is given to both the parties for termination of distributorship by issuing clear 30 days notice and this provision is applicable for either of the parties. It is not the case of the opposite party that the agreement has been entered into by coercion or fraud or by taking any undue influence over the other party. So, in absence of such allegation the stipulation made in Article Clause 9(B) of the agreement is to be taken as it is whereby both the parties has got option to terminate the said agreement. 

 9. It is not in dispute that section 7Ka of the arbitration Act, 2001 empowers the Court to issue any order restraining any party for any appropriate reason. But for invocation of this provision prima facie case needs to make out for restraining other parties. In the instant case the stipulation made in Clause 9(B) is very much clear and as such before issuing any order it was obligatory upon the Court to look into the stipulation made between the parties. It is apparent that the opposite party meanwhile issued notice under Clause 15 of the Arbitration Agreement for resolution of the disputes and if the petitioner disagrees in appointing Arbitrator, the opposite party has got option to come to the Court for appointment of Arbitrator for resolution of disputes, if there be any. 

 10. Apart from this in private commercial transaction the parties could terminate a contract even without assigning any reasons with a reasonable period of notice in terms of such a Clause in the agreement. In the case of Humayun M Vohra vs ESPN Star Sports 55 DLR (AD) 99 it is held that, 

 "temporary injunction cannot be granted in case of violation of contract for which adequate remedy can be had through compensation."

 13. Now, regarding the decision of 16 BLC 140 as referred by Mr Bhuiyan, there was an agreement regarding supply of goods and respondent No. 6 purchased and took delivery of majority of the goods from respondent No. 2 and as such the Court granted injunction with the observation that if the injunction is not granted the seller will be released from the delivery of the goods. The decision reported in 21 BLC 122 is relating to the tender and Bank guarantee and it was contended that for termination of the contract the arbitration clause does not get parished if the disputes survives as per the clause of the contract. But in the instant case since either party has got option to terminate agency by issuing clear 30 days notice, there should not be any restraintment order and as such the decisions as referred by Mr Bhuiyan are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the agreement has been terminated by issuing clear 30 days notice as per the provision embodied in the agreement. Continuation of Miscellaneous case is thus a fruitless litigation. 

 14. In the above context, I find merit in the Rule and accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. Order dated 9-10-2017 passed by learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous case No. 544 of 2017 is hereby set-aside. However there is no hindrance for opposite party to proceed with arbitration case if he so intends.
